discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees would make the electronic bands nearly flat. In that regime, interactions would dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero realized this prediction experimentally. He developed the tear-and-stack technique for precise twist control and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, all tunable with a gate voltage. This tight loop between theory and experiment created twistronics. It is now a universal platform where a single device can be tuned through strongly correlated, superconducting, magnetic and topological phases. Spectroscopic imaging, transport and optics in many laboratories have reproduced and extended these results. They have led to orbital ferromagnetism, Chern insulators and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in moiré materials. Few discoveries in the past decade have changed how we create and study strongly correlated quantum matter as much as this one.
